depth.transferChallenge: Write `fn retries(config: &Config) -> Option<u32>` using `?` on `config.network.as_ref()` instead of `and_then`. Then change the return type to `Result<u32, String>` and use `ok_or` to say which field was missing.

writing.exampleCaption: `and_then` follows the optional chain and `unwrap_or` supplies the `??` default, so `Some(0)` stays `0`.
writing.explanation:
TypeScript with `strictNullChecks` already marks absence as `T | undefined`, but the value can still be `null`, `undefined` or a missing property, and the checks vanish at runtime. Rust has no null. A value that may be missing has type `Option<T>`, which is either `Some(value)` or `None`, and you cannot use it as a `T` until you decide what absence means. `network.retries + 1` with an `Option<u32>` is a compile error, not `NaN`.

The operators become methods. `a?.b` is `a.as_ref().and_then(|a| a.b)` when `b` is itself optional, and `.map(...)` when it is not. `x ?? 3` is `x.unwrap_or(3)`, or `unwrap_or_else(|| ...)` when the default is expensive to build. Inside a function that returns `Option`, `let n = config.network.as_ref()?;` returns `None` early, the closest thing to optional chaining across statements.

There is no `||` default. `retries || 3` turns a configured `0` into `3`, and `title || "Untitled"` discards an intentionally empty string. `unwrap_or` only replaces `None`, so `Some(0)` stays `0`. If zero really should count as missing, say so with `.filter(|&n| n != 0)` and a comment.

`Option` answers whether something is there; it does not say why not. When the caller needs a reason, such as "storage unreachable" rather than "no such user", return `Result<T, E>`, or `Result<Option<T>, E>` when missing is a normal outcome and failure is a separate one. That replaces returning `null` from one path and throwing from another.
writing.feedback: `Ok(Some(t))` means found, `Ok(None)` simply missing, and `Err(e)` carries the reason the lookup itself failed.
writing.question: A lookup finds nothing when the key is missing, and fails when the storage is unreachable. Which return type gives the caller both facts?

recall.answer: `0`, then `5`, then `Some(1)`. `unwrap_or` replaces only `None`, like `??`, so the present zero is kept. `map` transforms the value inside `Some` and would leave a `None` as `None`.

recall.answer: `and_then` takes the `Option` by value, which would move `network` out of a struct you only borrowed: E0507. Call `config.network.as_ref()` first to get an `Option<&Network>`; then `n.retries` copies the `Option<u32>` out through the reference.

writing.rule: Use `Option<T>` when a value may be absent and `Result<T, E>` when the caller needs the reason; `unwrap_or` replaces `??`, not `||`.
writing.success: The local compiler accepts the changed solution and the separate verification harness passes every case, including a configured `0` and an empty title. Printing a success message alone does not complete this lab.
writing.summary: `null` and `undefined` become `Option<T>`: absence is part of the type, and `?.` and `??` become `and_then`, `map` and `unwrap_or`.

A missing settings value or field uses the default (20, `Untitled`), but a configured `0` or an empty title is kept, exactly as `??` does.
